subsystems.name: Feedstock and electricity
subsystems.role: supplies the carbon, hydrogen and energy the microbes need.

subsystems.name: Bioreactor
subsystems.role: the vessel where gases are dissolved and microbes grow.

subsystems.name: Microbial catalyst
subsystems.role: engineered bacteria or yeast that convert carbon and hydrogen into protein.
parts: strain with gas- or methanol-utilisation pathway

subsystems.name: Downstream processing
subsystems.role: harvests cells and turns them into a safe, stable protein ingredient.

subsystems.name: Formulation and texturing
subsystems.role: shapes the protein into meat- or dairy-like foods.

subsystems.name: Quality and safety
subsystems.role: checks that every batch is consistent and food-safe.

buildSteps.title: Capture carbon
buildSteps.detail: Concentrated CO2 is captured from an industrial flue gas stream or from the air, then cleaned of contaminants.

buildSteps.title: Make hydrogen
buildSteps.detail: Renewable electricity splits water in an electrolyser into hydrogen and oxygen.

buildSteps.title: Prepare nutrients
buildSteps.detail: Minerals, vitamins and trace elements are mixed into a sterile growth medium.

buildSteps.title: Grow the seed culture
buildSteps.detail: A small starter culture of the engineered microbe is stepped up in progressively larger vessels.

buildSteps.title: Run gas fermentation
buildSteps.detail: CO2, hydrogen and oxygen are fed into the bioreactor; the microbes multiply and build amino-acid chains, while temperature and pH are held steady.

buildSteps.title: Harvest the biomass
buildSteps.detail: The broth is centrifuged to separate the protein-rich cells from the liquid.

buildSteps.title: Break cells and extract protein
buildSteps.detail: Cells are disrupted mechanically or enzymatically, then the protein is filtered and purified.

buildSteps.title: Dry and formulate
buildSteps.detail: The protein is spray-dried into a powder and blended with fats, binders and flavours, then texturised into food products.

buildSteps.title: Scale up and approve
buildSteps.detail: The process is moved to larger bioreactors and the resulting ingredient goes through novel-food regulatory review.

prerequisites.why: electrolysis and fermentation both need large amounts of cheap, low-carbon power.
they provide the hydrogen that the microbes use as their energy source.
capture from flue gas is mature; direct air capture is still expensive and small-scale.
strains exist, but improving growth rates and protein yields remains active research.
centrifuges, filters and dryers are standard in the food and pharmaceutical industries.
approval routes exist in some markets but are evolving and vary by country.

pathway.milestone: pilot plants producing single-cell protein from CO2 and electricity, with first food approvals.
pathway.unlocks: proof that the biology and processing work outside the lab.

pathway.milestone: larger fermentation plants and falling production costs.
pathway.unlocks: ingredients that can compete with conventional protein on price.

pathway.milestone: engineered strains that secrete specific dairy or meat proteins.
pathway.unlocks: simpler purification and products that match familiar tastes and textures.

pathway.milestone: integration with direct air capture and dedicated renewable power.
pathway.unlocks: protein production largely decoupled from land, weather and animals.
